post.summary: Enable or disable automatic investigation of new blocked internal runs
post.description: Requires internal operator membership and the organization rollout flag. Enabling selects the caller as operator and one connected Composal source. The enrollment timestamp excludes earlier blocks. Disabling prevents queued automatic launches; active turns can be cancelled through their repair API. Automatic intake admits at most three investigations per organization per UTC day, using normal Roder limits and tools.

post.summary: Post a swarm worker's stack and receive its receipt
post.description: Requires a run capability carrying the swarm.submit_stack operation. One receipt per attempt: an identical replay answers 200 with the existing receipt, a different payload for the same attempt is 409 stack_payload_conflict, and a new payload behind the swarm's generation is 409 attempt_fenced. Bodies over 25 MiB, declared or decoded, are 413 stack_too_large before any receipt exists. input_revision and notice target_tip values are original 40-character Git commit IDs. Change keys retain their stable 32-character hex or reverse-hex spelling; SHA-256 evidence digests remain 64-character hex values.

post.summary: Attach a swarm worker's transcript to its stack's Changes
post.description: Requires a run capability carrying the swarm.submit_stack operation. The body names the opaque session and checkpoint identities, the archive's declared sizes and SHA-256 digests, and the zlib archive as base64. Idempotent: a replay finds the same session and checkpoint and re-appends the same native attachments.

post.description: Requires the server-held turn capability delegated by Roder. Browser session capabilities, browser cookies, and personal access tokens are not accepted. Returns a short-lived repository credential for the org Home checkout and a short-lived system personal access token that authenticates API/CLI calls as the spawning user. Both expire together and are reissued on refresh.

post.summary: Read current OCE native device routing admission
post.description: Namespace-scoped ingress-service protocol. A relay credential may read the currently authorized computer and selected OCE runtime only inside its current organization and namespace generation. Only established socket renewals may request a bounded cancellation-settlement window after a grant changes; new sockets, transfers and execution remain strictly admitted. It cannot mint a native bootstrap, execute commands or use an operator bridge. Native device, worker and transfer credentials remain mandatory.

post.description: Private native admission hook. Tenant bridge credentials and host-supplied native identities are required; background jobs recheck their persisted subscription. An optional canonical input run ID resolves the live web requester membership. This metadata does not authorize device execution; unknown inputs and background jobs have no device requester. An optional device request checks the bound sender against the exact device, native key, grant revision, capability, pairing generation and server environment. Device consent is a current product check only; it issues no execution credential and does not replace native invocation authority, leases or local consent.

200.description: Without `chunk`: the transcript index state — when `state` is `ready` the `manifest` and the per-chunk `chunks` URLs are included, otherwise only `state`, `session_id`, and `checkpoint_id`. With `chunk`: that chunk object's raw JSON, zstd-encoded when the client accepts it.

get.summary: Derived transcript index for one checkpoint (manifest + chunk bytes)
get.description: Returns the derived, chunked transcript index for one of the session's checkpoints: the manifest inline plus a same-origin URL per chunk. Those URLs point back at this same operation with `chunk=<seq>` appended, which serves the chunk object's bytes through the API — object storage answers signed GETs without CORS headers, so no signed URL is minted or returned here. When `checkpoint` is omitted the session's latest uploaded checkpoint is used. While the index is still being derived (or a build failed) the response is a bare `{state}` body (`preparing`/`failed`) and a build is lazily enqueued; poll until `state` is `ready`. Chunk bytes are zstd-compressed JSON: a client that advertises `zstd` in `Accept-Encoding` gets the stored bytes with `content-encoding: zstd`, any other client gets the same JSON decompressed. Chunk responses are immutable and cacheable (`private, max-age=86400, immutable`) because chunk objects are content-addressed.

parameters.description: Opaque cache token from the patchset's `diff_path`. It is not a capability — every request is authorized like any other read of the change. A fingerprint that no longer matches still returns the current diff, but without the `immutable` directive.

200.description: One patchset and its stored file diffs

404.description: The change or the patchset number does not exist

get.summary: Read the stored diff of one patchset, with patch bodies
get.description:
Serves the patch text Rails persisted when the patchset was submitted, so viewing a patchset's own diff never depends on jj-backend recomputing it. The change page carries file summaries only and names this path as `diff_path` on each patchset.
The fingerprint segment covers everything that determines the bytes, including the diff serialization version, so a body that changes is retired by moving to a new path rather than by a cache entry expiring. A request whose fingerprint matches is therefore answered `immutable` for a year. Request the `diff_path` the change page gave you; do not construct this path.

parameters.description: Override the base commit (defaults to the commit's first parent)

200.description: One commit range and its file diff

get.summary: File diff for one commit range, with no commit metadata
get.description:
The file bytes of a commit range and nothing a `users` row can touch. The fingerprint segment covers everything that determines those bytes — the repository, the virtual-repository subtree and patch byte budget, the two commits, and the diff serialization version — so a body that changes is retired by moving to a new path rather than by a cache entry expiring. A request whose fingerprint matches a range named by full commit ids is answered `immutable` for a year.
A range whose base is a moving reference, or a fingerprint that no longer matches, still returns the current diff but is not frozen.
Request the `diff_path` the commit page gave you; do not construct this path.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Override the base commit (defaults to the commit's first parent)

200.description: Commit metadata and the path serving its file diff

get.summary: Commit metadata for the commit page, and where its file bytes live
get.description:
The commit page's own request. It carries the commit's message, author, and resolved avatar — everything about the commit that a `users` row can move — together with `diff_path`, the fingerprinted path serving the file bytes.
This response revalidates and is never `immutable`: an author changing their profile picture changes it without any commit id changing, so no URL could express the change. The file bytes are addressed separately for exactly that reason, and can therefore be frozen.
Request `diff_path` as given; do not construct it.

post.summary: Create a short-lived voice companion call credential
post.description: Requires the same message permission and active, ready Clawder agent as sending a message, checked before and after provider IO. Uses the platform OpenAI credential server-side; only the ephemeral client secret is returned. Accepts no configuration or query parameters. The server configures a realtime voice companion with only ask_agent, which the browser delegates to the existing chat runtime and answers with its actual full response as function_call_output. The voice companion summarizes results briefly; it must not invent answers, progress, or outcomes. The secret expires after 60 seconds for establishing a connection; an established provider session may outlive it, and provider session settings are not an authorization boundary. Limited to 20 requests per user per minute, independently of push-to-talk transcription.

post.description: Requires the same message permission and active, ready Clawder agent as sending a message, checked before and after provider IO. Uses the platform OpenAI credential server-side; only the ephemeral client secret is returned. Accepts no configuration or query parameters. The server configures a realtime voice companion with only ask_agent, which the browser delegates to the existing chat runtime and answers with its actual full response as function_call_output. The voice companion summarizes results briefly; it must not invent answers, progress, or outcomes. The secret expires after 60 seconds for establishing a connection; an established provider session may outlive it, and provider session settings are not an authorization boundary. Limited to 20 requests per user per minute, independently of push-to-talk transcription.

The cursor is the signal's monotonic id carried as its public id (`sig_…`): `asc` (default) pages forward with `after_id` (exclusive), `desc` pages newest-first with `before_id` (`after_id` is accepted as an alias for the `desc` boundary so a caller can flip `order` alone). queue_position.description: The entry's place in the merge queue while it is still in it.

landed_commit.description: The first twelve characters of the commit the closure landed as.

AgentSwarmCreatePayload.description: PRD 146: the goal form (`goal` + `repository`) starts a planned swarm; the legacy `tasks[]` form materializes a one-level tree. One of `goal` or `tasks` is required.

base_bookmark.description: An existing bookmark to start from and land on; the plain form of `target.kind = bookmark`.

target.description: Where the swarm lands. `trunk` is the repository's default branch; `bookmark` an existing bookmark named by `name`; `new_bookmark` a bookmark named by `name` that the launch creates at trunk's head. Every worker starts from the target's head and every Change is opened against it; its merge queue is found or created on the first landing.

base_revision.description: 64-hex commit id; skips the head lookup

policy.description: Every key is optional and defaults to AgentSwarm::POLICY_DEFAULTS.

models.description: Per-role model overrides; roles left out keep the platform defaults.

pricing_version.description: The price table in effect now; rows carry the version they were priced at.

days.description: One cell per (day, model), ascending by day then model. Days with no usage are absent.

users.description: One row per (person, model), descending by tokens. `user` is null for hosted agents.

user_days.description: One cell per (day, person), ascending by day. `user` is null for hosted agents.

model.description: Provider model id; '' when the checkpoint reported none.

estimated_cost_usd.description: Decimal USD summed from each row's capture-time price.

unpriced_tokens.description: Tokens in `total_tokens` whose model had no list price, so the cost is a floor when non-zero.

body.description: Markdown text, or null until staff grant the organization access.

draft.description: The autosaved working copy of the newest Markdown version; null for older versions and other files.

content.description: Null when nothing has been edited since the newest version.

document_key.description: Stable document identity shared by all revisions.

package_options.description: Ready offers for initial enrollment. Omitted by API versions predating plan selection during a rolling release.

plan_selection_available.description: Whether to show the plan picker instead of continuing with an accepted package.

custom_pricing_available.description: Whether the plan picker includes a Custom contact option.

coupon_entry_available.description: Enter a legacy package coupon before opening Stripe. Prepaid packages accept promotion codes in Stripe instead.

limit.description: Decimal quantities are serialized as strings

upgrade_path.description: Frontend path of the organization's billing page

purchase_rejected.description: True only when this request identity is durably rejected and cannot later be accepted. Otherwise retain the identity for recovery.

extra_spend_enabled.description: Organization consent to paid overages across all metered usage.

preview.description: Metronome draft invoice and credits, or null.

breakdown.description: The 24-hour live series with its provenance; null only when the rollup fallback itself failed.

feature_enabled.description: Whether the `billing` feature is on for this organization. False renders the page as not enabled, with no Subscribe action.

credit_balance_cents.description: Remaining credit that offsets the draft.

metronome_invoice_id.description: Metronome's id for the invoice it pushed

ci_included_spend_cents.description: Monthly USD credit in cents shared by all CI charges, including runners, cache, storage and add-ons; replaces CI unit allowances when positive. Omitted by older API releases.

purchasable.description: Whether new purchases are available. Older API releases omit this field; absence preserves purchase availability.

projected_overage_cents.description: Forecast overage for the current allowance window.

raw_used.description: Full billing-period usage before allowance resets.

allowance_pool.description: Shared dollar allowance covering this meter. Omitted by older API releases.

spend_cents.description: What this period's overage costs so far at the unit price. The standard CI runner classes split their shared pool's overage by each class's own minutes.

cap.description: The quantity past which new usage is refused; null means unlimited.

period_spend_cents.description: Overage spend so far this period across every meter

ci_overage_cents.description: Net overage from the shared CI dollar pool; zero without a CI dollar allowance. Omitted by older API releases.

ci_projected_overage_cents.description: Forecast net overage from the shared CI dollar pool. Omitted by older API releases.

ci_uncapped.description: CI runner usage has no minute cap under the current package and extra-spend setting. Omitted by older API releases.

ci_spend_cents.description: Total CI spend before the monthly USD credit in cents, including runner, cache, storage and add-on charges. Omitted by older API releases.

ci_raw_used.description: Full-period CI usage with the shared standard pool counted once.

dimension_value.description: Empty for meters without a dimension.

subjects.description: Empty when no meter was given or the source is `rollup`.

wait.description: Only screenshots support wait: true. Complete the durable capture within this request; a lost response can be recovered using the same idempotency key.

partial.description: Retained footage has a capture failure or reported omissions.

source.description: Screenshot provenance. Dimensions describe retained PNG pixels. URLs are observations before and after capture; concurrent navigation may change the page during that interval.

playback_url.description: Authorized video capability, limited to five minutes and remaining retention. Refresh by reading this capture again.

authentication_status.description: Session readiness alone does not confirm application sign-in.

authentication_task_id.description: Automatic sign-in task; read its status and result separately from browser readiness.

closure_basis.description: Provider deletion is a conservative closure bound when the worker cannot report its stop time.

cdp_url.description: Admin-only full browser CDP bearer capability for the current external control generation.

expected_generation.description: The authorization generation displayed on the unfinished account.

cache_archive_observations.description: Bounded server response history; it does not confirm runner extraction or test-result reuse.

title.description: Short title: the native name, or the first prompt's first line without the agent's task preamble.

archived.description: Archived on its computer: hidden from the active list and shown with the archived threads.

section.description: Server-assigned section in the ordered computer thread directory.

reply_with_final_answer.description: True always forwards a final answer; false disables it. Null uses native replies and the original parent-reporting default for agent-created threads.

creating_operation_id.description: Original operation that registered this alias, retained when its address is reused. Inspect with agent.rename_status.

value.description: Ephemeral OpenAI client secret; keep private and never log it

acting_login.description: The GitHub login requests appear under while acting as the owner.

restriction.description: Why the viewer cannot turn acting as the owner on; null when they can.

size.description: Up to 3840 pixels on either edge, with a combined limit of 12,582,912 pixels per request. Auto uses the maximum per-image size for admission.

ClawderAgentSlackAsYou.description: The agent posting to Slack as its owner, with the owner's own Slack account through Composio.

can_manage.description: Only the owner may connect, configure or disconnect it.

mode.description: Which way the agent posts once the owner connected: as the owner (you) or with its own bot (bot). While it is you, the bot's Slack tools are not used. Null before the owner connects.

posting.description: Whether the agent posts as the owner now: mode is you, the organization allows the account here, and it is still saved. The bot cannot send while this is true, even when the account needs reconnecting.

callback.description: Desktop sign-ins return to a page that needs no session.

mode.description: Sent on its own: post as the owner, or with the agent's bot while keeping the account.

bot_name.description: The bot's name in Slack, as setup created it, once the app is configured

snoozed_until.description: When a snoozed thread returns to its usual group; null when it is not snoozed. Clients list rows with this set in their own Snoozed group.

group.description: Rails-owned list group, in precedence order: attention, active run, coordination custody, then done. A snoozed thread lists as done, after every other row, and never folds under Older; snoozed_until marks it. Rows retain server order; only done rows may fold under Older.

coordination_status.description: Durable work not represented by a native run: a queued input or an outstanding thread report.

attention.description: Why the person should open this thread: a pending question, the agent asking for attention, or a run that did not finish.

older.description: Nothing needs the person here, it is not working, and it has not changed for a day; the list folds it under Older.

execution.description: device_folder threads also report state and path; sandbox threads run on their own machine with the coding agent in harness.

repository_id.description: The repository a sandbox thread's machine clones, when it has one.

branch.description: The branch a sandbox thread's last workspace check saw. Absent after newer activity, until the next check.

base_branch.description: The branch a sandbox thread's machine cloned, when it was started from one.

model.description: The model a sandbox thread the agent started runs, from its recorded selection.

model_label.description: The display name of model, such as Claude Opus 5.5. Name the thread's author with it, not the coding agent.

environment.description: The repository's current setup state, only for a sandbox thread that started without a ready environment.

parent_conversation_title.description: Source conversation title, resolved independently of this page.

archived_count.description: Exact total of archived conversations for this agent, including subagents but excluding workflow task, cron and system sessions. Null or omitted when the runtime cannot establish the complete total without an unbounded archive read; never a loaded-page count.

local_status_pending.description: A computer is reporting newer local thread statuses; read the page again shortly.

local_activities.description: First page only: states of local threads listed on later pages, by local thread id, so a refresh keeps paged rows current.

local_archived_count.description: Local Claude Code and Codex threads archived on their computers.

total_archived_count.description: archived_count plus local_archived_count, computed by Rails for the Archived heading. Null whenever archived_count is unknown.

first_input_key.description: Idempotency-Key that finds the first message through input_delivery. Present with first_input.

first_input_requester_membership_id.description: Membership the first message was sent as, for input_delivery. Absent when it is bound to none.

owned.description: Whether the requester owns this computer and can remove its projects.

can_browse_folders.description: Whether the requester can list this computer's folders.

projects.description: Visible recent project folders, most recent first.

selected_folders.description: Configured folder shortcuts for new threads; empty when all folders are visible.

sandbox_harnesses.description: Coding agents a new sandbox thread can use now: codex plus each one whose credential is available. Present only for private bots.

empty_folder_harnesses.description: Coding agents a thread can use in an empty folder, with no repository. Present only for private bots.

sandbox_repositories.description: Granted, available repositories a new sandbox thread can start on, in grant order. ready means it starts from the repository's environment image. Present only for private bots.

harnesses.description: Coding agents a thread on this repository can use now, default first. A repository that isn't set up runs Codex only.

threads.description: Only when conversation_id is sent; kept for Composal Desktop 0.1.24 and earlier.

recipient.description: The send or ask stage's recipient as parsed by Lobster, including unresolved workflow arguments. Null when unavailable; omitted by older workers and non-message stages.

detail.description: The agent stage's prompt, the sandbox stage's command, or the send or ask stage's message.

thinking.description: The agent stage's reasoning, when it sets one; otherwise the agent's default.

granted.description: Whether this agent holds the grant now. Rails checks repository_write and pull_request_write against the agent's work repository grants and GitHub connections; a grant it cannot check is false.

environments.description: Sandbox environment per granted repository ID, shared by every bot granted that repository.

repository_choices_error.description: GitHub discovery warning. Saved grants and known local repository choices remain available.

can_prepare.description: Whether this person can start preparing the environment now. False while it is preparing, building or ready, unless a ready environment has a failed_update, and for people who cannot manage the bot.

can_check_branch.description: Whether this person can check this repository's environment recipe on a branch through Prepare. Needs a bot they manage and only they can use, in an organization with sandbox threads. Only in the repositories read.

status.description: none has no recipe build yet; preparing is a setup run writing the recipe; unsupported declares something bots cannot use, such as secrets; ready is the promoted revision thread sandboxes start from.

failed_update.description: Only when ready. The repository's newest recipe on its default branch failed to build, so threads still start from the ready revision. Prepare builds it again.

setup.description: The latest setup run until a recipe revision exists, only when this bot ran it; other bots see the status alone. Prepare with a branch answers with the branch check it started.

conversation_id.description: The setup or check thread's conversation, once it started

branch.description: The branch a check builds and proves. Only in the answer to the Prepare that started the check; the repositories read never shows a check.

configuration_state.description: The requested managed skill selection is awaiting runtime qualification.

reasoning.description: One of the model's reasoning levels in the Composal catalog. Omit or null for the runtime default.

credit_wait.description: The wallet funding an enabled routine that is waiting for inference credit.

https.description: Whether the organization's certificate serves this site over HTTPS

total_count.description: Total visible recorded openings when scope is opened.

email.description: Account email supplied by the subscription provider, when available. Separate from the editable label.

usable.description: Whether Rails can bill this account now. Absent on older API replicas.

saved.description: A personal saved account reusable on other owned private agents.

can_disconnect.description: Whether this account is attached to the current agent.

reasoning.description: Effort levels this plan model accepts.

speeds.description: Speed modes advertised by this connected account and model. Missing metadata enables Standard only.

ready_providers.description: Providers with an account that can bill now. Absent on older API replicas.

selection_ready.description: Whether the selected subscription is attached and ready for this private agent.

profile_id.description: Account to bill. Omit to let Rails choose: the account in use for this provider, else its first usable one.

reasoning.description: Effort for the plan model, one of the model's reasoning levels. Omit for the model default.

provider.description: Storage backend. `local_nvme` is a directory on the node's own NVMe, created as a Nomad dynamic host volume — fast, node-local and EPHEMERAL: the platform may delete it at any time and it does not survive the loss of its node. Use it as a cache, never as a system of record. `local_nvme_authority` is a single-node, single-writer authority volume that refuses destructive repair. Node loss requires restoration from remote replication into a new volume.

provider.description: Storage backend. `local_nvme` volumes are node-local NVMe caches and are EPHEMERAL by contract — deletable at any time, gone with their node, and safe to lose. They ignore capacity_gb (it is advisory) and are not resizable. `local_nvme_authority` provisions one pinned single-writer directory and refuses destructive repair or empty replacement after node loss. Remote replication and fenced restoration are required for repository authority durability.

payload.description: Exact signed JSON array: ["composal-coding-control",1,organization_id,device_id,pairing_generation,unix_milliseconds,nonce_hex_32,action,arguments,environment]. Signature is unpadded base64url Ed25519 over these UTF-8 bytes; timestamp must be within 15 seconds. Actions: connect {transports?}, pending {providers?,features?}, claim {operation_id,request_digest,provider?,features?}, finish {operation_id,request_digest,claim_token,response}. Omitted providers/provider select legacy Codex only. Desktop requests feature relay_mcp_v1 only when connect advertises it; an agent-attributed create then returns a source-bound MCP connection with a separate opaque bearer. Automatic native Relay deliveries require relay_delivery_wait_v1, advertised by connect and sent on both pending and claim. Their pending metadata contains relay_delivery {thread_id,mode:wait,expires_at}; Desktop checks native availability before claiming and retains one original queued receipt while busy. Parent-only actions native_plan {connection} and native_surface {connection} return DeviceAgentNodePlan and DeviceAgentNodeSurface respectively; surface approval follows native advertisement and the coding signer retains only connect/pending/claim/finish. Browser credentials do not replace this proof.

Repository must be currently selected and readable by the controlling user at publication with an exactly matching name. Item IDs and Sentry organization/issue identities must be unique. Completed work requires failing-before and passing-after verification for every item.

group.description: Optional grouping of 1–20 individual results, people or changes. Each field is one item and contributes exactly one to the displayed count, not an attribute of a single result. For people, label is the person's display name and value describes their outcome. Omit group for ordinary report attributes. Action is a short past-tense verb; subject is the noun phrase agreeing with the item count; provider is a toolkit name or null. Counts are derived by Rails, never submitted.

Optional grouping of 1–20 individual results. Each field contributes one item; never repeat a Sentry organization_slug/issue_id even through different accounts. Counts are derived by Rails, never submitted.

needs_attention.description: Failed or exception work that no one has marked handled since this revision

can_mark_handled.description: The viewer can manage this agent and the work needs attention

coding_summary.description: Combined completed coding outcomes at one delivery stage. Count is the total submitted items; collection count remains the number of saved results.

runtime_versions.description: Runtime choices authorized for this organization.

cost_tier.description: Relative usage cost from 1 (cheapest) to 4, from list prices. Null when unpriced. Absent on older API replicas.

repository_choices.description: Empty compatibility field. Use the agent's clawder/repositories endpoint.

PersistentAgentClawderInteraction.description: A registered interaction, one variant per kind. Choice, records, changes and form cards each require their own payload, and a records question its actions; every other kind shares the common fields.

PersistentAgentClawderStandingWriteAppro.description: Present when a standing write permission approved the write as it was requested, so no one was asked. The response is that approval.

PersistentAgentClawderChoice.description: Required for choice. The question's options as the agent supplied them; at most one is recommended and none is preselected.

submit_label.description: What sending the answer starts, such as "Open a PR for this fix".

PersistentAgentClawderInteractionFields.description: Durable registered interaction, at most 16 KiB serialized UTF-8, 144 KiB for agent_create, or 300 KiB for a bounded skill_install review. Transcript references grant no authority; use current server capabilities. Connection enablement saves a pinned local grant atomically with the receipt. Skill installation saves the decision before external import; processing is not an installed claim. Delivery status is independent of the accepted answer and application status.

id.description: Durable request ID; at most 256 UTF-8 bytes.

conversation_id.description: Explicit conversation identity, including an agent-scoped native session alias.

payload.description: Validated non-secret payload, at most 8 KiB serialized UTF-8, 16 KiB for records, changes and form, 128 KiB for agent_create, or 272 KiB for skill_install with a skill_bundle of at most 256 KiB, plus source_icon_url where present. New_agent is required for agent_create and contains the exact settings and grants to review. Connection is required for connection_enable. Repository and expected_version are required for repository_access. Agent and expected_version are required for agent_archive. Slack is required for slack_connect and reflects the signed-in viewer's own Slack link. Skill_bundle is required for skill_install and contains the exact pinned files to review. Resource identities come from Rails, never model input.

shared_by.description: Optional only for skill_install in main chat. Trusted source bot identity supplied by Rails, never model input.

verify_target.description: Required for verify_run. What Start runs, read by Rails from the prepared run; scenario_names lists at most the first 10.

verify_deep_scan.description: Required for verify_deep_scan. What Start scans, named by Rails; the description is the scan's goal. A null account_name scans signed out.

source.description: Optional for choice. The tool the agent read the options from, linked back to it. Agent-supplied, so the link is only ever https.

source_icon_url.description: For a choice with a source, for records, changes and form. The icon of the site the source links to, served through the platform's signed preview proxy. Absent when the link has no host to read.

records.description: Required for records. Rows the agent read from a tool and the ask actions the person may take on the rows they tick. Agent-supplied, so links are only ever https.

changes.description: Required for changes. Exactly what a write will change, which the person approves item by item before the agent runs it. Agent-supplied, so links are only ever https.

allowed_for_agent.description: Only for changes, when a standing write permission approved the write; its shape is in PersistentAgentClawderChangesInteraction.

form.description: Required for form. Content the agent drafted for a write, which the person edits and approves before the agent writes it. Agent-supplied, so links are only ever https.

slack_message.description: Required for slack_message. Where the message goes, as Rails pinned it; the description is the exact text, sent as the agent's owner once they approve it.

channel_name.description: The channel's name in Slack, without

show_sent_using.description: Whether Composal adds "Sent using Composal" under the message.

verify_project.description: Required for verify_project_access. The Verify project approval adds to the agent's grants, named by Rails.

workspace_name.description: Connected Composal Slack app workspace, if installed.

account_connected.description: Whether the signed-in viewer has linked their own Slack account.

connect_url.description: Composal Slack install/link endpoint. Opens Slack OAuth in a separate tab; use it only when capabilities.can_connect is true.

identity_label.description: Current verified provider account/workspace label, only visible to its custodian. Not a grant or saved decision.

can_connect.description: connection_connect: the viewer can start provider authorization. slack_connect: the viewer can open the Slack install/link flow now.

can_always_allow.description: changes: the viewer manages the agent and Rails does not always preview this tool, so their approval may also allow its writes with this tool, as this account, from now on (always_allow).

PersistentAgentClawderAgentCreation.description: Exact settings for agent_create. Approval creates a V2 agent owned by the signed-in approver and installs the pinned team apps. Credentials and personal connections are never copied.

identity_label.description: Current verified provider account/workspace label, only visible to its custodian. Not a grant or saved decision.

tool.description: The tool the agent writes with, such as linear.update_issue.

account.description: Whose account the writes run as, as the preview named it, such as Maya Chen through Linear.

in_effect.description: Whether the permission approves writes now. False once the person who gave it can no longer manage the agent.

selected_skills.description: Required only for skill_install; unique subset of reviewed names, nonempty when confirmed and empty when declined. Forbidden for other kinds.

action.description: Required only for a confirmed records, changes or form answer; the id of the action pressed. Forbidden otherwise.

always_allow.description: Only for a confirmed changes answer from a viewer with can_always_allow. Also lets the agent make its writes with this tool, as this account, without a preview from now on, until someone who manages it removes the permission. Deletes and payments, and changes that cannot be undone, are flagged, run SQL or start left out, are still previewed; email sends, sharing and member changes are not. Forbidden otherwise.

choices.description: Required for choice, records, changes and form. For choice, the picked option values in option order; one value for a single choice, one or more for a multiple choice. For records, the ticked record ids in card order, which the action decides. For changes, the ids of the included items in card order, at least one. For a form batch, the ids of the kept drafts in card order, at least one; empty for a single draft. Empty when skipped with confirmed false. Forbidden for other kinds.

values.description: Required only for a confirmed answer to a single form draft. Every field as the person approved it, which may differ from the draft. Forbidden otherwise.

items.description: Required only for a confirmed answer to a form batch. Each kept draft with every field as the person approved it, in the order of choices. Forbidden otherwise.

url.description: Public HTTPS GitHub tree URL pinned to revision, optionally scoped to a skill directory.

PersistentAgentClawderSkillBundle.description: Immutable bridge-resolved review bundle, at most 256 KiB serialized UTF-8. Installation imports these exact bytes without fetching the source again.

content.description: Full SKILL.md UTF-8 text, at most 128 KiB.

selected.description: Initial review selection; not human approval.

files.description: Companion files excluding SKILL.md; at most 128 files per skill including SKILL.md.

path.description: Unique safe UTF-8 relative path inside this skill directory, at most 512 bytes and 255 bytes per component. Spaces and Unicode are preserved; no traversal, controls, backslashes or SKILL.md.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text, at most 128 KiB.

PersistentAgentClawderSkillInstallResult.description: Verified per-skill receipt, at most 24 KiB serialized UTF-8, covering exactly the human-selected names.

error.description: Single-line non-secret failure explanation without control characters, at most 1000 UTF-8 bytes, only for failed entries.

actor_name.description: The name of the person who answered, for the card's stamp. Absent when their profile has no name.

result.description: Present only when a confirmed agent creation, grant, archive or Verify run start committed, or a skill import returned its verified per-skill receipt. Absent while a skill import is processing or uncertain. Not a claim about current access.

oneOf.description: The Verify run a verify_run approval started.
The deep scan a verify_deep_scan approval started, and its page.
What happened to an approved slack_message. uncertain means Slack may have it; it is never resent.
The Verify project a verify_project_access approval granted.

PersistentAgentClawderInteractionCancelI.description: Exact JSON body, at most 4 KiB serialized UTF-8. The idempotency key is bound to actor, request, operation, expected revision, and canonical validated body.

PersistentAgentClawderInteractionRespons.description: Exact JSON body, at most 4 KiB serialized UTF-8 (8 KiB for skill_install). A confirmation grants nothing. Confirming agent_create creates a V2 agent owned by the signed-in approver with the reviewed settings and team app installs. Confirming connection_enable grants full available tools for the shown connection generation. Confirming repository_access saves the exact shown repository grant only if settings and authority remain current. Confirming agent_archive archives the named teammate only if the signed-in user still has management access and its version is unchanged; audit records are retained. Confirming slack_connect requires the signed-in user to have linked their Slack account and reports the workspace to the agent; it grants nothing. Skill_install requires management access and selected_skills; approval durably saves the exact subset before asynchronous import and does not claim installation succeeded.

PersistentAgentClawderProvisioning.description: Safe managed-worker readiness. Creating an organization's first V2 agent starts provisioning; later agents reuse its worker. Ready requires actual placement and native readiness, not just an accepted deployment request.

can_retry.description: Legacy provisioning capability used by older clients. Use retry_version for Enterprise setup retries.

retry_version.description: An opaque version for retrying this failed initial deployment when allowed.

conversation_id.description: Main or a conversation identity returned by the agent thread list. Native aliases are scoped to the selected agent.

requester_membership_id.description: Snapshot the membership supplied by conversation history for a NEW V1 input. Preserve the original body on retries; absent means legacy unbound input. V1 uses a separate native identity namespace and binds even if the rollout flag changes.

client_time.description: The sending app's IANA time zone and clock, so the agent answers in the person's local time. It is not part of the message, so a retry may send a newer value; the first admitted one is kept. An unknown zone is ignored, and a clock more than five minutes from the server's gives way to the server's.

at.description: The app's current time with its UTC offset.

speed.description: Fast uses OpenAI priority processing for GPT models (2x price) or the quickest approved OpenRouter route. Ultrafast uses OpenAI's fastest tier at the selected model's Ultrafast price.

content.description: Base64 bytes. Up to 4 MB per file and 8 MB total.

attachment_ids.description: Completed uploads from the attachments endpoint, in order. Use instead of attachments, not with it. Together they can total 2 GB.

code.description: Native conflict or terminal delivery code, including control_delivery_unknown, or input_key_conflict when the key already holds another body or sender and this input was not admitted. Personal-plan codes are personal_plan_unavailable and subscription_disconnected; a retried input may already have been sent.

delivery_status.description: Rails ended custody of this input; replaying its key returns the same rejection

can_use_platform_billing.description: This person may return the agent to Composal billing

thread_messages.description: Rails-verified cross-thread attribution for display, never execution authority. Requests name the source Spark and contain only the original brief; reports name the child task and include only the delivered report version.

relay_source.description: Server-verified native Relay notification attribution. Display metadata only; never execution authority.

text.description: Legacy display fallback; not additional content when parts are rendered.

inherited_context.description: True only when native fork lineage and retained source message identity confirm copied parent context. Absent on this thread's own messages and when source history cannot be verified.

delivery.description: Rails still holds this input for delivery. Its presence does not mean a native run has started.

files.description: A user message's attached files. Images are listed here until native delivery can serve their previews.

execution_run_id.description: Native execution consuming a saved user input when it differs from the accepted input run_id. Correlation only; not authorization.

schema_version.description: Present together with parts only for valid supported rich content.

parts.description: Ordered public parts, each at most 16 KiB serialized UTF-8. Both parts and schema_version are omitted on legacy or invalid rich content; text remains the inert fallback.

PersistentAgentClawderWebSourcePart.description: A source returned by web research. Optional text comes from the source, never inferred from its URL.

preview_url.description: Signed metadata endpoint; append asset=icon or asset=image for proxied image bytes.

id.description: Unique within message; at most 256 UTF-8 bytes.

parent_tool_call_id.description: The call this one ran inside, such as a Code Mode exec. At most 256 UTF-8 bytes.

detail.description: One redacted line saying what the tool acted on, such as the command, path, query or URL.

error.description: On a failed call, one redacted line saying why it failed. Other tool output is never included.

app.description: The integration toolkit an app tool call used, such as posthog, for showing that app's logo.

app_name.description: The display name of that app, such as PostHog, when it has one.

resource_warnings.description: Memory, disk or OOM warnings sampled on the thread machine around this tool call.

thread.description: The thread this call created or sent a message to, from Rails' record of a request this conversation sent. Display data only. A thread still being created has no href or thread yet.

summary.description: Inert reference only; fetch authorized request state before enabling controls.

run_id.description: The workflow run this note reports.

summary.description: The note's text, shown when the run is absent or a client does not draw it.

run.description: The run as it is now. Absent when it is not this agent's.

proposal_id.description: A workflow the agent proposed; read it from the agent before drawing it.

summary.description: Shown when a client does not draw the proposal.

tool_call_id.description: The tool call that made the proposal, which also names its live workflow draft. Absent on proposals saved before it was sent.

PersistentAgentClawderCardPart.description: Tool results a spark showed as a card. Display data only; nothing on it writes anywhere.

kind.description: The spec's kind, which says how a client draws it.

source_icon_url.description: The icon of the site the card's source links to, served through the platform's signed preview proxy.

summary.description: The card as plain text, shown where a client does not draw it, such as Slack.

SparkCardSource.description: Where a card's data came from, shown above it with a link back.

SparkCardProblem.description: Why a card is empty, failed or partial, in the spark's words, with the tool's own message.

SparkCardTruncation.description: How much of the tool's data the card shows, and why the rest was left out.

SparkRunStep.description: One step of a run as the tool reported it. Steps nest at most three levels, and every id in a run is unique.

log_tail.description: The last lines of the step's log, verbatim. highlight indexes the lines that say what failed.

SparkRunSpec.description: A run of any tool, such as a CI workflow, a deployment or a test scenario, and its steps. Its status agrees with its steps, and it has steps unless the read came back empty or failed.

SparkStackTraceFrame.description: One frame of a trace. in_app and context are known only with source maps, and a context's highlight is one of its lines.

in_app.description: Whether the frame is the team's own code.

SparkStackTraceSpec.description: An error and its stack trace, frames innermost first. Without source maps (symbolicated false) no frame has in_app or context and there is no suspect commit; with them every frame says whether it is in_app.

message.description: Empty when the error had none, as new Error() does.

symbolicated.description: Whether the tool had source maps.

chained.description: The exceptions that caused this one, each with its own frames.

breadcrumbs.description: What happened before it threw, oldest first.

suspect_commit.description: The commit the spark thinks caused it, shown as its inference.

SparkDiffFile.description: One file of a change. Only a renamed file has old_path, and a binary file or one the spark did not read has no hunks.

lines.description: Each line as [op, text], op " " for context, "+" added or "-" removed.

items.description: [op, text]. Not a prefixItems tuple: openapi-fetch reads tuples as plain arrays, so readers check op.

unread_reason.description: Why the spark could not read this file, so it never looks clean.

SparkDiffComment.description: The spark's comment on a line one of its file's hunks shows on that side.

SparkDiffSpec.description: A change's files and hunks, with the spark's comments anchored to the lines they are about. Paths and comment ids are unique.

SparkFunnelSpec.description: A funnel as the tool reported it. Steps are in order, each count at most the step before's, previous_count is on every step or none along with previous_period and never with a breakdown, and each breakdown group has one count per step.

window.description: The conversion window, such as "within 7 days".

previous_period.description: The period previous_count is from, such as "Previous 7 days".

SparkChartUnit.description: What a value is in. percent is 0 to 100, currency is in major units, and a custom unit names its suffix.

one.description: The suffix for exactly 1, such as "pt" for "pts".

SparkChartDimension.description: What x, or a matrix's rows or columns, are. grain is for time only.

timezone.description: The IANA zone instants are shown in, such as America/Los_Angeles.

SparkChartX.description: An x value. A date (2026-11-12) for a day or week grain, a month (2026-11) for a month grain, an RFC 3339 instant for a finer grain or none, a number on a number axis, and a label for a category.

SparkChartSpec.description: Data from a tool and a description of it; clients derive the form, scales and labels. Each point is [x, y] or [x, y, low, high] with x fitting spec.x and low ≤ y ≤ high; a matrix has one value per row and column.

subheading.description: The range, such as "Hourly, last 24 hours".

items.description: [x, y] or [x, y, low, high]; a null y is a gap.

annotations.description: Releases, incidents and notes on a time or number x axis; a chart of categories has none.

SparkCardInference.description: The spark's judgement, shown apart from what the tool returned.

one.description: custom only, the suffix for exactly 1, such as pt.

priority.description: 1 stays at every width. Defaults to 1 for title, id and status, 2 for subtitle and 3 otherwise.

SparkRecordsValue.description: A value typed by its field; null when the tool had none.

signals.description: Facts from the tool worth a second look, worst first.

proof.description: Screenshots that show the record's work working, from the spark's own Library.

url.description: The download path library_publish returned. Clients show it only for the spark that owns it.

video.description: A screen recording's download path, when url is the screenshot of its final state.

SparkRecordsSpec.description: Rows a spark read from a tool, as a list, one record in detail, a board grouped by a field, or a table. The client chooses the layout and formatting.

width.description: contained keeps the card in the conversation's reading column. full spreads it across the conversation pane for wide tables.

group_order.description: The board's columns in order, including empty ones. Groups that records name and this omits follow it.

evidence.description: The query or request that produced the rows, shown collapsed under a table.

select.description: Whether the person can tick one row or several for an action. Only on a records interaction.

actions.description: What the person can ask the spark to do next. Only on a records interaction, never on a card part.

label.description: May contain {n}, the number of ticked rows, and {noun}, the spec's noun for that number.

SparkChangesFieldChange.description: One field of a record, before and after the write. Values are typed like a records field.

type.description: How the values are typed, as in a records field. Without it they are plain text.

SparkChangesItem.description: One thing the write changes. A record update lists its field changes; a statement gives its text and effect.

included.description: Whether the item starts ticked. Defaults to true; the person can untick it.

irreversible.description: Set on an item that loses something. Approving an included one takes one more step that names the loss.

flag.description: Why a person should look at this item twice.

SparkChangesSpec.description: Exactly what a write will change, item by item, shown before the person approves it. The spark runs the write after the approval, on the items the person kept and with the values shown.

verb.description: What the write does to each item, such as Move, Resolve or Apply.

untouched.description: What the write deliberately leaves alone.

revision.description: What the preview was computed against, so the spark can refuse a write once it has moved.

label.description: May contain {n}, the number of included items, and {noun}, the spec's noun for that number.

tool.description: The tool the spark calls after an approval, such as linear.update_issue.

as.description: Whose account the write runs as, such as Maya Chen through Linear.

SparkFormValue.description: What a form field holds, for the field's type. Text, longtext, markdown, choice, date and datetime are strings; a datetime without an offset is wall-clock time in the viewer's zone. Number is a number, boolean true or false, multichoice and labels lists of strings, and person {person, id?}. Null when empty.

value.description: Sent back as the answer; a person option's value is the person's id.

recommended.description: The spark's suggestion, shown in words and never preselected.

disabled_reason.description: Why it cannot be picked; the option shows but is disabled.

SparkFormField.description: One thing the draft says. The client picks the control from the type and options.

max_length.description: text and longtext or markdown only; at most 500 for text.

allow_other.description: choice and multichoice only. The person may type an answer that is not an option.

options_source.description: person only. The options are a few of many people in the tool, so the person may type another name, which the spark looks up there.

SparkFormItem.description: One draft of a batch, with its own values. Its first field's value names it.

excluded.description: Starts unticked; the person can tick it.

SparkFormSpec.description: Content the spark drafted for a write, for the person to edit and approve before the spark writes it. One draft is a set of fields; a batch repeats the same fields per item, each of which can be left out.

heading.description: What is drafted, such as "New Linear issue".

subheading.description: Where it goes, such as "Platform team".

items.description: A batch. Fields then carry no value; the first field is text and names each item.

label.description: May contain {n}, the number of included items, and {noun}, the spec's noun for that number.

tool.description: The tool the spark calls with the approved draft, such as linear.create_issue.

as.description: Whose account the write runs as, such as Maya Chen through Linear.

done.description: What the card says once approved, in the past tense, such as "Created {n} {noun}".

secondary.description: An action that drops the draft, such as Discard. Nothing is written.

ClawderBrowserContext.description: Advisory snapshot of the browser pane beside this conversation when the message was sent.

url.description: HTTP(S) origin and path with query and fragment removed.

target_id.description: CDP identifier for the selected remote tab. Reference only.

model.description: Effective model reported by the native conversation, including inherited selections. Null when unavailable.

label.description: Display name of model, such as Claude Opus 5.5.

billing.description: Present when an applied personal subscription governs the next turn.

input_run_id.description: Identity computed for the optional Idempotency-Key header. Does not confirm native acceptance.

requester_membership_id.description: Current authenticated membership offered for new V1 inputs. Does not authorize execution.

can_queue_input.description: Current authority to admit a durable input independently of native readiness.

pending_question.description: The question this conversation's agent is waiting on, asked with ask_user.

waiting_runs.description: On the main conversation's latest page, the agent's workflow runs a step stopped for the person.

stopped_runs.description: On the main conversation's latest page, the viewer's notices of this agent's workflow runs that stopped without finishing, newest first.

id.description: The notice, which the workspace activity dismissal endpoint dismisses.

message.description: One line naming the workflow and why it stopped.

at.description: Explicit UTC offset; instant must be exactly representable at microsecond precision.

anchor.description: Explicit UTC offset; instant must be exactly representable at microsecond precision.

expression.description: Five-field cron; repeated local hours use the first UTC instant.

timezone.description: Explicit IANA time zone, matching the cron zone when applicable.

grace_seconds.description: Explicit late one-shot grace. Recurring downtime coalesces to one occurrence; resume skips the unclaimed backlog through its saved boundary.

requester_membership_id.description: Current authenticated membership offered for new V1 inputs. Does not authorize execution.

can_queue_input.description: Current authority to admit a durable input independently of native readiness.

text.description: Cumulative display preview bounded to 128 KiB of UTF-8. Does not replace the native receipt.

PersistentAgentClawderStreamRenew.description: The stream is about to end on purpose, for example to reload history the live stream could not send. Reconnect at once for a fresh snapshot.

PersistentAgentClawderStreamQuestion.description: Sent when the conversation's agent asks a question or one is answered; carries the next pending question, or null.

PersistentAgentClawderStreamReasoning.description: The current step of a run's reasoning, sent when it changes. Progress only; it is not saved to the transcript.

PersistentAgentClawderStreamWorkflowDraf.description: A workflow the agent is still writing in a workflow proposal, drawn from what it has written so far. Progress only; it is neither checked nor saved, and the proposal the tool returns replaces it.

PersistentAgentClawderStreamAgentBrowser.description: The agent asks the client to show the user a live view of the agent's own browser, which the user can control. A separate event so older clients, which do not listen for it, ignore it.

PersistentAgentClawderStreamUiAction.description: The agent asks the desktop app to show the user a place in its own UI, such as a settings control. Clients that do not listen for it ignore it.

text.description: Full native wire snapshot. Takes precedence over delta_text.

PreviewResourceOverrides.description: Service public IDs mapped to resource overrides. Omitted fields inherit; an empty map removes all local overrides. Null reservations select platform defaults.

provider_private_endpoint.description: Captured managed data resource advertises a provider-private endpoint; no endpoint or credential material is included.

first_task.description: The first job they would hand an agent. Optional.

invite_code.description: The referral code of the invite link they arrived through.

website.description: Honeypot. Render it hidden and leave it empty; any value discards the request.

referral_code.description: Shared in this entry's invite link.

position_after_next_referral.description: The place one more referral would give this entry, as Rails would assign it.

total.description: Display total including a random increment per signup; not the actual number of entries.

referral_count.description: People who joined through this entry's link.

places_per_referral.description: Most places one referral moves the entry up; fewer when boosted entries are ahead.

account_name.description: Project-scoped display name, present in page and state-detail projections.

revision_name.description: Project-scoped environment and revision display name, present in page and state-detail projections.

connections_loaded.description: Whether transitions, attempts and unresolved controls have been loaded.

map_version.description: Project change watermark captured before connection loading; null for screens-only responses.

demo.description: A signup's demo project, copied from the Acme Notes template. Archiving removes it.

managed_google_available.description: Whether this administrator can add or reuse the shared Google account for this website project.

managed_google_email.description: The shared Google test account's email address.

sign_in_check_apps.description: The project's apps a credential's live sign-in check can run on; empty when checks are unavailable.

url.description: The app's address, so people can tell similar apps apart.

latest_sign_in_checks.description: Each credential's most recent sign-in check today, if any.

reason.description: Why a waiting, blocked or stopped check needs the person, in the agent's words: its question or first blocker. Null otherwise.

composal_address_suffix.description: What follows the chosen user part in a new Composal email address, for example @acme.mailposal.com. Null while new addresses come from the legacy mail provider, which names them itself.

identity_provider.description: Where the organization's apps trust Composal sign-in, for new personas

state_options.description: Lifecycle totals matching the search, across all priorities and pages

priority_options.description: Priority totals matching the search and selected lifecycle, across all pages

run_options.description: The 100 most recent runs with findings, plus the authorized selected run even if older or empty

findings.description: Findings from scenario runs, Discoveries and Deep Scans, highest priority first, then most recently seen

locked.description: True for a locked finding of the workspace's included scan before it pays. Its title, source title and verification reason are empty.

source.description: The workflow that produced the finding

source_title.description: The scenario, Discovery or Deep Scan that produced the finding

web_path.description: Where the finding is reviewed within its source

PersonaSummary.description: A persona with its credential, scenario count, runs in flight and recent outcomes across every scenario it carries out

attention.description: What needs an operator's eye, problems before notices

scenario_id.description: Null for a run of a scenario file, which is not saved as a scenario

outcome.description: The state once the run has finished
