gaps.description: What the recording could not show.

persona_hint.description: signs_in when the journey signed in but its persona does not.

SessionShowMarker.description: A commit landmark. Rails resolves `event_index` against the transcript being shown. Emitted only for checkpoints whose index is built. The commit the checkpoint was sealed at rides along: `git_commit_sha` (with `github_commit_url` when the repository is still addressable on GitHub) and `linked_commit_ids` open Git commits associated with this checkpoint. A checkpoint with no commit association carries neither.

git_commit_sha.description: 40-hex Git commit this checkpoint was sealed at; null when unsealed.

github_commit_url.description: Where that commit lives on GitHub, built from the repository's GitHub address. Null when the checkpoint is unsealed or the repository has no GitHub address.

SessionShowTokenStats.description: Session-level token usage for the header cost estimate. `total_tokens` and `token_usage_scope` are the non-additive session aggregate; `token_usage` carries the itemized counters and `model_usage` the per-model split behind it, resolved with the same scope rule. `subagent_token_usage` is the child-agent share already inside them. `model` is from the latest uploaded checkpoint. The flat per-type fields remain for readers of the older shape.

SessionTranscriptStats.description: Derived header stats for the resolved checkpoint's transcript. File/line/ duration fields are null when derivation could not read them (the UI omits those); transcript facet counts are always present.

SessionShowTranscriptIndexState.description: The resolved checkpoint's transcript-index build state (page contract).

session.description: Identical serialization to the org sessions page's expanded session, so the web reuses one session-detail builder. Jump-to data lives in `markers`, not on these checkpoints.

TranscriptIndexBucketCounts.description: Event counts by UI filter bucket. Prompts include user, system, and developer messages. Responses, reasoning, tool traffic, and other lifecycle data remain distinct. Drives both whole-transcript totals and precise per-chunk skip planning during backward loading.

event_start.description: 0-based inclusive index of the first event in the chunk.

event_end.description: 0-based inclusive index of the last event in the chunk.

bytes.description: Uncompressed JSON byte size of the chunk.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the uncompressed chunk JSON.

url.description: Same-origin API path for the chunk's bytes — this operation with the resolved checkpoint pinned. The version and digest identify the exact immutable chunk bytes. Relative, so the browser sends it to the API with its session credentials.

TranscriptIndexChunk.description: One chunk object's body, returned when `chunk` is set. Served zstd-encoded to clients that accept it, decompressed to everyone else.

chunks.description: Per-chunk same-origin URLs, present only when `state` is `ready`.

avatar_url.description: Avatar URL for the session owner: their OAuth/profile picture when set, otherwise a deterministic Gravatar derived from their email (mirrors History's commit author avatars).

AgentTokenUsage.description: Itemized token counters a cost estimate prices. `input_tokens` is the uncached prompt share; `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` are the two cache classes (priced very differently), with the creation count split by TTL when the provider reports it; `cached_input_tokens` is their sum. `output_tokens` already includes `reasoning_output_tokens`. `api_call_count` is the number of distinct model responses behind the counters. Each field is null when the harness did not report it.

AgentCostEstimate.description: Estimated token cost at today's public list prices, priced by Rails so no client carries a price table. `usd` is a decimal string. `floor` is true when a model in the session has no list price, so the figure is a lower bound; those models are listed in `unpriced_models`. `models` gives each priced model's share. Rows shipped to analytics carry the price at capture time instead, so history never moves when the table does.

model.description: Provider model id this share of the usage was billed to.

token_usage.description: Itemized counters behind `total_tokens`, resolved across uploaded checkpoints with the same scope rule. Null when no checkpoint reported usage.

model_usage.description: Per-model split of `token_usage`, sorted by model. Empty when the checkpoints predate per-model accounting.

message_count.description: Conversation prompt and response count derived from the session's latest uploaded checkpoint transcript. Falls back to the captured harness count when the transcript has not been indexed, or null.

agent_count.description: Total agents the session ran (the primary agent plus its observed child agents), or null for a solo session with no observed subagents.

model.description: Model id from the latest uploaded checkpoint, for cost estimation.

commit_count.description: Server-derived Git commits linked to this session. The commits themselves ride the expanded session, not the row.

pull_request_count.description: Distinct GitHub pull requests those commits belong to. Zero while a trailer link is waiting for its pull request.

pull_requests.description: The first few of those pull requests, in first-seen order, so a row can link them — at most three, whatever `pull_request_count` says. A reader renders the remainder as a `+N` from the count.

evidence.description: How the server found this commit for the session: `trailer` — the commit message carried the session's `Vex-Session` line; `merge` — GitHub reported it as the pull request's merge commit. `checkpoint` — a session's checkpoint was sealed at this commit and no trailer named it.

pull_request_number.description: The pull request this commit was found in, or null for a trailer link discovered before any pull request named it.

github_url.description: The pull request on GitHub, built from the virtual repository's owner and name. Null when that addressing is missing.

merge_commit_sha.description: The commit that landed on merge, whatever strategy produced it.

harness.description: Harness id the session presents as (codex, claude-code, cursor, roder, grok): the captured envelope's harness when recorded, else the adapter's canonical harness.

last_activity_at.description: When the session last did anything: the newest checkpoint capture, else the session end, else its start.

model.description: Model id from this checkpoint's sanitized envelope, or null.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort from this checkpoint's sanitized envelope (none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra), or null.

total_tokens.description: This checkpoint's own reported token total, or null.

token_usage_scope.description: What the reported total covers (turn, session, or cumulative), or null when no usage was reported.

linked_commits.description: Native commit ids this checkpoint is attached to (reverse checkpoint→commit lookup). Empty when unavailable or unattached.

linked_commits_available.description: True when the reverse checkpoint→commit lookup succeeded for this session; false (with empty `linked_commits`) when it was unavailable.

original_resume.description: An author-only local resume target for the original provider session. Null for other viewers and unsupported providers.

linked_commits_available.description: True when the reverse checkpoint→commit lookup succeeded for the expanded session; false when it was unavailable.

total_tokens.description: Session token headline: the latest checkpoint's own reported total (never a sum — turn and cumulative scopes are not additive), or null when no checkpoint reported usage.

token_usage_scope.description: The scope of the headline total (turn, session, or cumulative).

token_usage.description: Itemized counters for the cost estimate, resolved across uploaded checkpoints with the session aggregation rule. Null when no uploaded checkpoint reported usage.

model_usage.description: Per-model split of `token_usage`, sorted by model.

models.description: Distinct model ids seen across the session's checkpoints, first-seen order.

redaction_count.description: Total redactions across the session's checkpoints.

linked_commits.description: Distinct Git commit IDs the session's checkpoints are attached to, in first-seen order. Empty when the reverse lookup was unavailable.

commits.description: Server-derived git commits for this session, oldest first, each labelled by how it was found.

pull_requests.description: Distinct GitHub pull requests those commits belong to, in first-seen order.

resume_checkpoint_id.description: Public id of the checkpoint a local resume/continue command should target — the latest UPLOADED checkpoint (only uploaded checkpoints have a verified archive). Null when none uploaded.

SignalIntegrationMode.description: `connected` is a customer-owned credential pasted into Vex; `managed` is a Vex-provisioned resource where Vex already holds the credential.

SignalIntegration.description: One organization's connection to a signal source. Secret values are never rendered; `webhook_secret_stored` / `api_token_stored` say only whether one exists.

inbound_url.description: The absolute URL to paste into the provider's webhook configuration.

unmapped_delivery_count.description: Deliveries accepted whose provider resource matched no enabled target.

rejected_signature_count.description: Deliveries rejected for a bad or missing signature.

SignalIntegrationTarget.description: One provider resource mapped to a hosted app. A delivery naming an unmapped resource still becomes a signal, with null attribution.

SignalIntegrationDelivery.description: One inbound receipt. Provider content is deliberately absent — the debugging question this answers is arrival, processing and failure.

delivery_id.description: The provider's delivery id, or a `content-…` id derived from the event kind, its timestamp header and the body checksum when it sends none.

ops_signal_id.description: Public id (`sig_…`) of the signal this delivery emitted.

webhook_secret.description: The provider's signing secret. Stored as an organization secret; never read back.

api_token.description: Optional provider API token for target discovery and backfill.

hosted_app_id.description: Hosted app public id (`app_…`), raw id, or slug.

OpsSignalLinks.description: Canonical, relative API paths built from real routes (docs §6a). Sits alongside — never inside — the frozen `payload`. A key is present only when it resolves from the columns the signal carries; `self` always is. These are REST resource paths, not UI routes.

external.description: The provider deep link for an integration-sourced signal — the one absolute URL in this envelope, present only when the payload carries an http(s) `external_url` (docs §6e).

OpsSignalResolution.description: Recovery pairing (docs §6b). Present only on signals with a pairing shape — `runtime.health` degraded/failed and `alert.fired`. An applicable-but-unrecovered signal renders just `{ "resolved": false }`; every other kind omits the key entirely.

resolved_by_signal.description: Public id (`sig_…`) of the signal that cleared the condition.

OpsSignalAttributionRef.description: One attribution target (hosted app or app service) — public id + display name.

OpsSignalAttribution.description: The producer-stamped attribution (docs §3) lifted out of `payload` into a typed sibling (docs §6d), so consumers get the ids and names they need — e.g. vex-web building its own UI routes — without reading the per-kind JSON. Always present; each key is null when the producer did not know it.

OpsSignalRecovery.description: Recovered/resolved state folded from the `resolution` pairing (docs §6b/§6d). Present only when the pairing is satisfied — `recovered` for a runtime.health signal whose instance came back to running, `resolved` for an alert.fired whose event cleared. Absent otherwise.

OpsSignalSourceProvider.description: Who produced the signal (docs §6e). `vex` is every signal the platform emits itself. Slack is the native Composal app; the others are signal-integration adapters.

OpsSignalSource.description: Provenance envelope (docs §6e), a sibling of the frozen `payload`. ALWAYS present, so a reader never branches on key presence: a Vex-produced signal renders `provider: "vex"` with null siblings.

integration_id.description: The `sint_…` public id of the signal integration that ingested this signal. Null for native Vex and Slack sources; Slack uses its same-organization SlackInstallation subject.

external_id.description: The provider's own id for the thing the signal is about (a Sentry issue id).

external_url.description: Deep link to read the full event at the provider — Vex stores only a bounded reduction of it. Mirrored as `links.external`.

SignalSubscriptionFilters.description: The frozen filter slice a `SignalSubscription` stores. `sources` is the roadmap-138 addition, normalized and validated exactly like `kinds`.

hosted_app_ids.description: Rendered as `app_…` public ids; accepted as public ids, raw ids, or slugs.

OpsSignalSolutionChange.description: The Change a linked agent run submitted as the fix (`link_signal_to_change`).

OpsSignalAgentRuns.description: Dispatched-run summary (docs §6c). Present only once a signal has at least one `SignalAgentRun`, of either origin.

OpsSignal.description: One ops signal, as serialized by `OpsSignalResource` (frozen envelope, docs §3). Every id is a prefixed public id, never a raw bigint.

id.description: The signal's own `sig_…` public id — also the paging cursor value.

kind.description: A frozen taxonomy kind (§1) or an `app.custom.*` kind.

payload.description: Per-kind shape (docs §4), with the producer's `region`/`app`/ `service` attribution keys baked in when known. Frozen contract — deliberately not narrowed per kind here.

summary.description: One-line, kind-composed human sentence for the feed row (docs §6d, e.g. `deploying → failed`, `47× fp_9c1e77a4b2d0f331`) — server-authored so consumers never re-derive it from `payload`.

occurred_at.description: ISO8601 domain event time — what the UI displays and `since` filters on.

acked_by.description: Who acked the signal, read from `acked_by_user_id`. Always present so it reads as a pair with `acked_at`: null while unacked, and null for an ack recorded without a user (a bulk ack from a token-authed caller).

created_at.description: ISO8601 row insert time — retention math and debugging only.

next_cursor.description: The last returned signal's public id when more pages exist, else null. Feed it back as the same boundary param the request used.

ids.description: Explicit `sig_…` ids. When present every other key is ignored.

before_id.description: Inclusive upper bound (`sig_…`) — ack matching signals at or before it.

source.description: Single source provider or comma-separated list (docs §6e). Alone it satisfies the "explicitly scoped" guard.

integration_id.description: One signal integration — raw id, or `sint_…` once that model ships.

all.description: Opt in to an otherwise-unconstrained ack of every unacked signal.

recovered_only.description: Narrow to signals whose `resolution.resolved` is true. Composes with every other filter and alone satisfies the "explicitly scoped" guard.

quoted_credits_cents.description: Grant shown for each refill, in usage cents.

billing_unit.description: Compute minute quote version returned by the billing summary.

top_up_step_cents.description: Minimum manual top-up and increment, in USD cents.

top_up_max_cents.description: Maximum manual top-up, in USD cents.

credits_cents.description: Included usage value in USD cents.

ToolFeedbackMetadata.description: Caller-supplied session context; no secrets or transcripts

source_ref.description: Opaque saved-content reference. It grants no access.

setup_required.description: True when the repository has no jj-backend counterpart yet, so the client should offer first-time setup instead of browsing.

transcripts_label.description: e.g. "3 transcripts". Null when no transcript is linkable.

checkpoints_label.description: e.g. "3 checkpoints". Null below two, where the count adds nothing.

tokens_label.description: Exact total with the scope it was measured over, e.g. "2,461,146 tokens (cumulative)". Null when no total is known.

status_label.description: e.g. "Still uploading". Null when the context is ready to read.

captures_label.description: e.g. "2 captures" when this session saved the commit more than once. Null for a single capture.

status_label.description: e.g. "Still uploading". Null when this transcript is ready to read.

VcsCommitChangeLink.description: The reviewable Change this commit landed from. Absent on commits that never went through review.

reference.description: The organization-scoped human id, rendered as `#262`.

landed_by_name.description: Display name of the user who landed the Change (or the Change author when landed_by is unset). Prefer this over the commit's author_name when the history line says "landed".

actor_name.description: The person the history line names — the Change lander when the commit has landed, otherwise the commit author.

actor_verb.description: The verb that belongs next to the actor. `landed` when this commit was observed as the target bookmark's tip.

ref_name.description: The ref this page walked — the requested `ref`, or the resolved trunk when the request named none.

default_branch.description: The repository's authoritative trunk, resolved server-side.

search_truncated.description: True when `q` stopped at the search scan bound rather than at the root of the repository, so "no matches" means "none this far back".

diff_path.description: Fingerprinted path serving this commit range's file diff. Rails builds it; fetch it as given rather than assembling one.

VcsCommitRangeDiffResponse.description: Carries no commit metadata by design — an author's avatar would make these bytes mutable and cost the response its `immutable` window.

generated.description: True when this path is a lockfile or well-known generated dump a reviewer usually does not need expanded.

directory_ref.description: Immutable commit reference for expanding this tree. Fall back to ref.name when absent.

loaded_directories.description: Directories whose children are present; null for a recursive index.

VcsActorSummary.description: Human user summary or organization automation identity. Automations have kind and slug, without email or picture_url.

VcsChangePatchsetUnresolvedCommentCount.description: Unresolved review threads on one file of one patchset.

VcsLabel.description: A free-form, organization-scoped grouping name applied to changes.

slug.description: Normalized identity used for filtering and lookup.

total_count.description: Total related changes for this label, which may exceed the returned page.

relation.description: Position of this member relative to the change being read.

overridable.description: True when an acknowledged override can clear this requirement.

VcsChangeLandingTone.description: Semantic readiness tone. React maps this to presentation; Rails never sends CSS.

evaluated_head.description: Full revision evaluated by the check.

VcsChangeLanding.description: Server-computed submitted-together closure and landing preflight. An unavailable closure returns `available: false` with `error` and nothing else.

target_requires_checks.description: Whether a bookmark protection rule makes the merge queue require CI on this target. When false, a deferred landing has nothing to wait for and lands immediately.

scope_version.description: Opaque fence echoed back as `expected_scope_version` when requesting a landing.

blocker_summary.description: One-line stack footer for why the set cannot land yet. Null when there are no requirements. Derived from requirement codes; React must not re-summarize the requirement list.

waiting_on.description: Ordered readiness rows for the land action preview.

sync_available.description: Whether Rails could build a merge preview for every Change in the landing scope.

available.description: True when this actor may force the set past its overridable requirements.

requirement_version.description: Opaque fence echoed back as `expected_requirement_version` when overriding.

version.description: Optimistic fence echoed back as `expected_version` when cancelling.

retry_count.description: How many times the queue restarted this attempt after it stalled.

health.description: Whether the retries so far are routine or the attempt is going nowhere.

failure.description: The error this entry itself recorded, verbatim.

queue_error.description: What the merge queue tick last recorded. Sent only while this entry is at the front of the queue, and attributed to the queue rather than to this change.

VcsChangeLandingFailure.description: A raw recorded error, shown behind a disclosure. Unlike the guidance summary this is the queue's own internal text and is not a fixed vocabulary.

retry_count.description: How many times the queue restarted this attempt before it stopped.

agent_prompt.description: A paste-ready prompt for a coding agent. Rails composes it from the published attention contract so the browser only copies it.

VcsStackLanding.description: Compact landing state for the Stack CLI.

lifecycle.description: Index badge. Stored status stays open while a change is in an active landing request (waiting) or a current ejected request (needs_attention). Filters still use status.

updated_at_label.description: Relative time since the last update

VcsPagination.description: Pagy's own page data. Navigate with `previous` and `next` rather than by adding to `page`, which the server may have resolved down to `last`.

from.description: Position of this page's first row in the whole scope. `0` when the page holds no rows — an empty scope, or a `page` past `last` — so treat `0` as "no range" rather than as a row position.

to.description: Position of this page's last row in the whole scope. `0` when the page holds no rows, for the same reason as `from`.

VcsOrganizationChangeListResult.description: The flat change queue. `pagination` counts changes.

VcsOrganizationChangeGroupSubject.description: What names one group. The `kind` matches the active grouping, except for the pinned `unstacked` remainder under stack grouping.

member_count.description: Every member of the stack, including those the active filters excluded.

started_at.description: Null for `older`, whose range has no lower bound.

ended_at.description: Null for `past_hour`, whose range is open above so a future timestamp is still reported.

key.description: Stable public key for this group — a stack code or `unstacked`, a user public id, or a period name. Echo it back in `group_pages` to move this group alone.

changes.description: One page of the matching changes in this group. Stack groups keep graph order, from tip to root; every other grouping uses the requested change sort.

VcsOrganizationChangeGroupedResult.description: The queue divided into groups. `pagination` counts group keys, not changes.

pagination.description: Null for `created_time`, which returns all four of its periods.

has_description.description: True when the change has Vex-owned review description content, distinct from the JJ commit message.

assets.description: Proof assets referenced from the description as `vex-asset:<id>`.

reviewer_candidates.description: Organization members available to the reviewer picker on this page.

VcsExpectedCiEstimate.description: Historical CI duration estimate for the pipelines expected to run for this submission, from recent terminal pipeline-run wall-clock times. Omitted entirely when no workflow matches, no terminal history exists, or the estimate could not be computed.

finding.description: What went wrong, in the operator's words.

workaround.description: What later runs should do instead.

reported.description: Whether the runner posted a learning report; false when the run was done entirely by the model without one.

replayed_steps.description: Learned steps replayed and checkpointed before the model took over.

offered_steps.description: Learned steps Verify offered this run, every fresh step whose digest matches; the model completes any step without one.

healed_actions.description: Replayed actions whose control had moved and was found again.

model_from_step.description: The zero-based step the model started from; null when replay completed every authored step.

offered_outcomes.description: Learned outcome checks Verify offered this run, every fresh outcome whose digest matches; they are checked once every step is complete.

replayed_outcomes.description: Offered outcomes whose learned checks passed without the model.

steps.description: How each journey step the run completed was done, in authored order. Steps the run never completed are left out.

mode.description: learned when replayed with no model call; healed when replayed and Decisions found at least one moved control again; ai when the model did it because nothing was learned or replay failed.

learned_from_run.description: The public id of the earlier passing run whose learned step this run replayed; null for ai steps, or when the dispatch did not record it.

actions.description: The actions this run took for the step, as reported for learning; empty when the step could not be learned.

checks.description: The passing checkpoint checks that proved the step; empty when the step could not be learned.

outcomes.description: How each outcome the run checked, passed or failed, was done, in authored order. Unchecked outcomes are left out.

mode.description: learned when its learned checks were replayed and then independently reviewed; ai when the model checked it.

learned_from_run.description: The public id of the earlier passing run whose learned checks this run replayed; null for ai outcomes, or when the dispatch did not record it.

checks.description: The live checks that proved the outcome; empty when it could not be learned.

ScenarioRunLearnedTarget.description: The signals that identify a control by its accessible role and name, not a CSS selector. Text is capped at 300 characters.

label.description: The control's accessible name.

context_text.description: Text around the control that tells it apart from similar ones.

ScenarioRunLearnedAction.description: One action a run took for a step. A fill of a granted credential names only its kind (value_ref_kind), never its value; a mailed sign-in code or link is read live from mail, never stored. Text is capped at 300 characters.

kind.description: upload chose files through a picker; mail_code filled the sign-in code mailed to the Persona; mail_link opened the mailed sign-in link.

value.description: A literal fill value; synthetic test data.

repeat.description: How many times in a row a page key press was pressed; null is once.

path.description: Where a navigation went, relative to the target.

files.description: The files an upload chose; null for other actions.

directory.description: Whether an upload chose a folder; null for other actions.

ScenarioRunLearnedVisualClick.description: Where a click on no identifiable control landed.

anchor.description: The nearest observed control, or null when there was none.

offset.description: The click in CSS px from the anchor's top-left corner.

point.description: The click as a fraction of the viewport.

ScenarioRunLearnedFile.description: One file an upload chose. A synthetic file's content is not shown.

source.description: fixture for a file attached to the Scenario; synthetic for a small text file the model generated.

name.description: The file's name, with {{run_tag}} for the run's own tag.

ScenarioRunLearnedCheck.description: One check that proved a step or outcome. Text is capped at 300 characters.

source_step_index.description: For an outcome about state a later step removed, the earlier step whose passing check proves it.

status.description: HTTP status of a failed request; 0 when it never got a response.

first_offset_ms.description: When it first happened, from the start of the recording.

occurrence_count.description: How many scenario runs and reports have raised this finding.

annotations.description: Numbered callouts on this exact screenshot for this outcome. Coordinates are fractions of the image, with the origin at its top left. Older runs may have none.

preview_url.description: Set for media a browser can show in place, such as screenshots.

findings.description: Findings this outcome raised. A scenario's findings come from its failed checks, so they are listed once, with its first failed outcome.

decision_screenshot_count.description: Number of distinct screenshots cited by the outcome decisions.

decided_by.description: Present when a model judged the outcome's text visible, or absent, in its checkpoint screenshots because the text capture could not read it. One entry per decision.

ScenarioRunLive.description: Latest browser activity while the ScenarioRun is running.

model_activity.description: Public agent summary and recent tool calls. Absent on older workers.

LiveBrowserStream.description: The live view of a running browser. The token authenticates the read-only video and event socket at url; devtools_url opens full Chrome DevTools and is null unless the viewer may run tests and the runner serves it.

cause_label.description: Who can fix the result, in words to show with the summary. Null when cause is null.

cause.description: Who can fix the result. app means the app did not meet an expected step or outcome; access, the sign-in account was refused; prerequisite, data or state the Scenario needs was missing; obstacle, the browser could not get past the page as the steps describe it; runner, Composal's runner failed; timed_out, the run ran out of time. Null when the run passed or gave no reason.

step_index.description: The authored step this entry checkpoints, by zero-based position; present only for a live journey's step entries.

outcome_index.description: The authored outcome this entry checks, by zero-based position; present only for outcome entries.

multi_actor.description: Multiple named actors own independent browsers in this scenario.

actor_id.description: The named actor whose browser this recording contains; null when unknown.

duration_ms.description: Recorded length of this segment of one continuous recording, when known.

events.description: Timestamped replay events with settled outcome verdicts; failed checks superseded by a passing review stay excluded. Computer-use recordings include native evidence reviews at their report capture times, with timed actions as a fallback.

phases.description: Recorded step and outcome spans, followed by terminal application cleanup when recorded. Computer-use recordings retain native action spans without inferring authored-step completion. Cleanup includes retries and time spent finalizing.

step_summary.description: The scenario's step list. Live journeys list every authored step, then each outcome the agent checked, in the order it checked them; a step the run never reached has status not_reached and no time, and an outcome row's status is that outcome's settled verdict, the same as its outcomes entry. Fixed replays list named plan actions.

outcome_index.description: The authored outcome's zero-based position, present only for outcome rows.

step_index.description: The authored step's zero-based position, present only for a live journey's step rows.

step_ids.description: Recorded step ids this row covers, in order.

actions.description: What the narration adds to this step, in order. An action is something the agent did or saw that the step does not say; a check is a failed attempt to confirm the step, labelled with what was seen. A met outcome lists no checks.

activity.description: The run's activity in plain words, in order. What the agent did and each authored step or outcome it checked, with retries of one step folded into a row and unlabelled runner steps left out; then what the browser and agent reported. Raw steps and observations stay in their own fields.

detail.description: For a failed check, what the agent saw instead; for a report, its original text.

attempts.description: How many times the agent tried this row.

browser_events.description: Left out when the run page is read with diagnostics=false.

dropped_browser_events.description: Left out when the run page is read with diagnostics=false.

replay_start_ms.description: Step-clock offset where replay opens, after the first step loads its page.

text.description: Bounded redacted request or response payload.

steps.description: The steps that ran, with their offset into the recording.

actor_id.description: Browser actor that produced this event, when known.

dropped_browser_events.description: Earlier browser events left out of browser_events.

available.description: Whether this deployment has a Slack app configured

workspace_name.description: The connected Slack workspace, or null when none is installed

account_connected.description: Whether the current user has linked their own Slack account

repository_count.description: Connected repositories Verify can test pull or merge requests for

viewer_url.description: Owner-only bearer link. Do not share; expires with the browser lease.

title.description: The page's title; the workspace's included scan is named for the app it tested, as in `Free scan of acme.example.com`.

startup_retryable.description: Whether the browser can retry startup within this run's remaining budget.

onboarding.description: Whether this is the workspace's included Deep Scan.

next_action.description: Null while the report is locked behind a plan.

finding_count.description: Findings at every priority; findings lists only the listed priority.

priority.description: The priority findings are narrowed to, or null when they are not narrowed.

finding_ids.description: Original team order used by legacy hash links and rerun indices.

unlock.description: Whether a paid plan would unlock some of this scan's findings, and whether this person may choose one.

available.description: True while some findings stay locked and Checkout can start for the workspace; anyone but an owner is asked to find one.

can_manage.description: Whether this person may choose a plan; only workspace owners manage billing.

url.description: The findings page to return to, and to share, for unlocking.

package_options.description: Plans the owner can choose at Checkout; empty when the workspace's assigned plan is used, or nothing is locked.

free_findings_pending.description: Whether a scan with locked findings has yet to choose which are free, so every row is locked for now. Keep checking while true; reviews don't affect it.

reruns_available.description: Whether findings can be rerun; a scan with locked findings waits for a paid plan.

environment_query.description: The search the environments match. Older API releases omit this additive field.

environments_has_more.description: More environments match than the 25 configured environments and 25 previews returned; false when environment_query was omitted. Older API releases omit this additive field.

capacity.description: Shared capacity when supplied by the API release. Older API releases omit this additive field during independent web and API rollouts.

concurrency_limit.description: Operator browser limit; null means no organization concurrency cap.

available_slots.description: Available operator-limited slots; null means no organization concurrency cap.

deep_scan_defaults.description: A signed-out browser Deep Scan's team when launched without budgets, before an environment is chosen. Older API releases omit this additive field.

preview.description: A short-lived pull request or branch deployment, listed after configured environments. Older API releases omit this additive field during independent web and API rollouts.

flow_map.description: Flows from the newest discovery; null until discovery has recorded some.

deep_scan_defaults.description: The team a signed-out Deep Scan of this environment gets without budgets. Older API releases omit this additive field.
The team a Deep Scan of this environment with this login gets without budgets. Older API releases omit this additive field.

waiting_runs.description: Finished runs and blocked executions the next dream will review

runs.description: Every run the dream covered, reviewed or skipped, so it can exceed the dream's reviewed count

changes.description: One page of changes when tab is changes; empty otherwise

runs.description: One page of covered runs, reviewed or skipped, when tab is runs; empty otherwise

timezone.description: Organization IANA timezone dreams are scheduled in

start_hour.description: Local 24-hour clock hour a dream starts

id.description: Public id used in the dream's URL

reviewed_date.description: Local day whose finished runs it reviewed

timezone.description: Organization timezone the dream used

phase.description: Where the dream is. queued: waiting for a worker. running: a worker holds it. stalled: marked running but no worker holds it. paused: it hit an error and the periodic sweep still resumes it. stopped: it hit an error and is no longer retried automatically; only an administrator can resume it. completed: finished normally. stopped_early: finished, but ended before reviewing everything because its project or environment became unavailable.

attention.description: The dream skipped at least one run, which will not be retried

reviewed.description: Finished runs and blocked executions reviewed, not counting skipped ones

skipped.description: Runs skipped after repeated rejected review output

changes.description: Knowledge and memory entries created, updated or archived

error_code.description: Diagnostic code from the last failure, or from a dream that stopped early; not display copy, show reason instead

reason.description: Plain-language explanation of the phase: the cause and what happens next. Null for queued, running and completed dreams.

window_start.description: Start of the reviewed local day

window_end.description: End of the reviewed local day

resumable.description: The dream failed or was interrupted and no worker holds it, so an administrator can resume it now

entry_id.description: Public id of the knowledge document or memory

reason.description: Why the dream made this change

previous.description: The entry before this change; null when the change created it

current.description: A memory as it is now, since memories have no page of their own; null for documents, which open their own page

can_add_back.description: True only when the dream archived this knowledge document, it is still archived, its previous title and Markdown were kept, and no available document in the project already has that title (compared ignoring case). Then its previous content can be added back as a new document. Always false for memories and for any other operation

restore.description: Present only when restoring this exact previous version is allowed

expected_digest.description: Send as expected_digest when updating the document

runs.description: Runs this change cites, at most five

outcome.description: The run's state as recorded, such as completed, partial, failed, passed or blocked

observed_at.description: When the run finished, a person triaged the finding, the pull request merged, or Verify first read an open pull request head

exploration_id.description: Discovery or Deep Scan page id; open /explorations/{id} for kind discovery and /deepscan/{id} for kind deep_scan

execution_id.description: Project run page id for a saved Scenario execution or a pull request's Verify run; open /runs/{id}

reason.description: Plain-language sentence for why a skipped run was not reviewed, null for other runs

messaging_tester_number.description: One configured tester number. Copied to each preview; may be overridden locally before preparation.

input.description: Scrubbed tool arguments, truncated to 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Absent on older workers.

output.description: Scrubbed tool result, truncated to 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Absent while pending or on older workers.

input.description: Scrubbed tool arguments. Absent on older workers.

output.description: Scrubbed tool result. Absent while pending or on older workers.

summary_sequence.description: Stable sequence of the current public summary's first chunk; absent on older workers.

tools.description: Up to twelve recent tool calls with scrubbed arguments and results when captured by the worker.

launch_options.description: Present only when launch was requested by an admin

deadline_at.description: When the team's time limit ends. Older API releases omit this additive field during independent web and API rollouts.

credential_name.description: The credential the team signed in with, by its saved name if it was deleted; null for public access. Older API releases omit this additive field.

scenario_count.description: Scenarios saved from this discovery. Older API releases omit this additive field.

scenarios_pending.description: Scenarios are still being prepared, so scenario_count may still grow. Older API releases omit this additive field.

onboarding.description: Whether this is the workspace's free first discovery, started by setup.

paywalled.description: Whether this is the workspace's included Deep Scan (verify_onboarding_deep_scan), or a rerun of it, while the workspace has not paid. Its chat and report are withheld and its findings list only free findings and finding stubs; its agents are listed as on any run.

unlock.description: Once a paywalled scan ends, whether a paid plan would unlock its locked findings and whether this person may choose one, as on its findings page. Null while it runs and for other runs.

finding_count.description: Findings at every priority, locked ones included.

covered_areas.description: Titles of the testers that reported checks, in team order; areas assigned to testers that never ran are left out.

time_limit_reached.description: Whether a partial run ended because it used its whole time budget, rather than stopping early.

ended_early.description: Whether a partial run stopped before its team did its work: no tester completed or reported a check and no agent reported a finding, as when the lead stopped at sign-in, or inference failed. False for a team that ran its course with a tester short of completed.

demo_project.description: The workspace's copy of the demo project, linked from the free first discovery as an example; null for other runs or without one.

startup_retryable.description: Failed browser startup can be retried without extending the original deadline or tester budget.

can_continue.description: Whether a finished run can be resumed through the orchestrator.

next_scan_improvements.description: The optional setup the first scan's page offers for a better next scan, in order: a test account for a run without one, a repository except for a Deep Scan, and a plan.

sign_in_outcome.description: A sign-in check's outcome; null for other runs.

sign_in_question.description: What a sign-in check's agent asked the person while it needs their answer; null otherwise and for other runs.

sign_in_needs_answer.description: Whether a sign-in check needs the person's answer next: its agent waits in its browser with no reply on the way, or the check ended on an unanswered question and an answer starts the agent again. False for other runs.

agent_filters.description: Status counts and matching agent IDs for every filter in this live snapshot.

observed_at.description: Time this run snapshot was read; distinct from browser activity timestamps.

title.description: The page's title; the workspace's included Deep Scan is named for the app it tested, as in `Free scan of acme.example.com`.

web_url.description: The run's page in the Composal web app

project_id.description: Set when the exploration targets a project environment.

reproduction_of.description: The Deep Scan or Discovery and reported bug this scan reruns in a fresh browser.

deep_scan.description: False when the rerun checks a bug a Discovery reported.

explorer_activity.description: What the team is doing now. The coordinator is not counted as an area.

phase.description: Discovery maps the app; Deep Scan coordinates investigations from existing knowledge. Workers investigate their areas and the coordinator reviews their reports.

active_areas.description: Areas in progress or waiting to start.

findings_fix_prompt.description: One coding-agent prompt covering every finding, most severe first. Null when there are no findings.

saves_scenarios.description: Whether this exploration has started saving scenarios. Deep scans never do.

scannable_flows.description: Flows a finished exploration recorded that deep scans can start from.

huntable_flows.description: Deprecated alias of scannable_flows, kept for released CLIs.

reproductions.description: Fresh-browser reruns of this scan's reported bugs.

findings.description: Every tester's findings, most severe first, with the checks each one cites.

checks.description: Checks in the same tester report that this finding cites.

fix_prompt.description: A coding-agent prompt for this finding alone

locked.description: True for a locked finding of the workspace's included scan before it pays. Its text fields are empty and its steps, checks and evidence are withheld.

area.description: On a locked finding, the first segment of the page it was seen on, such as Billing.

has_recording.description: On a locked finding, whether the tester recorded evidence for it.

confirmed.description: On a locked finding, whether the automatic review confirmed it.

tracked.description: The finding record to resolve or ignore; null until the tester finishes.

orchestrator_id.description: Root orchestrator for this task; null when its owner is unavailable.

title.description: Compact charter excerpt; the complete instructions remain in charter.

model_selection.description: Immutable model-blend draw recorded at admission; absent on single-model and historical runs.

finding_count.description: Findings this agent reported itself; a review's restated findings count on the tester that observed them.

review.description: Whether this orchestrator reviews the testers' reports rather than starting investigations or mapping the application.

review_summary.description: For a review, what it concluded without repeating its testers' passing checks; null for any other agent.

attention.description: The review's checks that did not pass, each with the tester that saw it, or null where the review saw it itself.

own_passed_check_indices.description: Positions of the passing checks the review made in its own browser.

stream.description: The live view while this tester's browser runs.

model_activity.description: Current public model summary while this task runs; null after it stops.

narration.description: The tester's steps in order. While it works, one line each time its live narration changed; once finished, its written-up account when it has one.

step.description: How many browser actions were done when the line began.

status.description: unknown when the line has no saved actions to judge.

thread_sequence.description: Monotonic checkpoint sequence for reconciling retained activity with live updates.

thread_activity.description: Retained public reasoning, tool status and scrubbed payloads for orchestrator rounds. Bounded to 200 entries and 256 KiB. Arguments and results are absent on older workers.

VerifySignInOutcome.description: What a sign-in check established. waiting: the agent asked the person something and waits in its browser. verified: the agent signed in with the account as saved now. settings_changed: it signed in, but the account changed afterwards. blocked: it could not sign in. firewall_blocked: a firewall or bot challenge kept its browser from the app. browser_failed: its browser never ran. stopped: the person stopped it.

max_seconds_limit.description: Maximum explicitly requested discovery duration in seconds.

no_sign_in.description: The person said the app has no sign-in; always false with an account.

starts_after_sign_in_check.description: Whether finishing setup with the chosen account waits for its sign-in check to pass before the workspace's included Deep Scan starts (verify_onboarding_deep_scan). When false, finishing starts what it starts at once, so the wizard waits for the person to start it.

status.description: Rails' decision. `awaiting_sign_in` means the workspace's included Deep Scan starts once the chosen test account's sign-in check passes. `starting` means Rails is starting the discovery, so the wizard keeps checking for it; `ready` means the user starts it.

discovery_id.description: The started first discovery. Rails sets it; the wizard opens it.

included_scan.description: Where the workspace's included scan stands once test access is chosen, and the one action the test account step offers. Null before access is chosen.

state.description: `checking` and `sign_in_needed` wait for the account's sign-in check: `checking` while its agent works, `sign_in_needed` once it needs the person (waiting for an answer, or failed). `firewall_blocked` means the app's firewall or bot challenge stopped the check's browser before the app. `creating_test_user` and `sign_up_stopped` are the same for a test user Verify's agent made: it is signing up, or it stopped and setup asks for an account instead, saying why in `reason`; `run_started` means Rails started a discovery instead (an account the Deep Scan can't use) while the first run waits for a plan; `plan_needed` means the included scan is no longer on offer and nothing runs.

action.description: Start (or retry) the scan, open `discovery_id`, or open the plan step. Null while Rails works.

path.description: Canonical web path for the run, Deep Scan or Discovery. Null before it starts.

reason.description: In one sentence: for `sign_up_stopped`, why the agent couldn't create a test user; for `firewall_blocked`, what stopped the browser. Null otherwise.

firewall.description: For `firewall_blocked`, whose firewall stopped the browser; `other` when unknown. Null otherwise.

refusal.description: Why the last start was refused. Finishing setup again retries.

signed_in.description: Signs in with the test account chosen in setup; false explores public pages only.

next_action.description: What a viewer can do next with the combined summary. Null while the report is locked behind a plan.

writer.description: The scenario writer checking this discovery's scenarios; null on the single-call path.

progress.description: Of the drafts saved for trial, how many are published and how many are on a revision.

found_bugs.description: Scenarios published as failing, each with the confirmed finding it found.

budget_stopped.description: The organization's daily browser budget stopped checking; Retry resumes it.

live_browsers.description: Trial browsers running now, at most four.

scenario_id.description: A held candidate's saved, unpublished draft.

VerifyExplorationReportPage.description: Report page data, excluding tester activity and full replay archives. Sources contain only cited files.

assignments.description: Every assignment with its target's name, including targets archived or disabled since.

VerifyFixtureUpdate.description: Each assignment list that is sent replaces that kind of assignment; omitted lists are kept.

project_id.description: Project slug or public ID the repositories are added to.

replace.description: Make these the project's only repositories. Refused when another of its repositories has PR testing set up.

origin.description: Operator edit, automatic review of one run, or nightly dreaming

dream_id.description: Public id of the nightly dream that made this change; null unless origin is dreaming

latest.description: The most recent dream for the selected project, or null before the first one

login_url.description: Optional sign-in path or URL. Runs use the selected environment origin and retain the path, query and fragment. Not required for oidc_identity. Imported session cookies still require their app URL.

email_link_auth_origins.description: Explicit auth-service origins for protected email-link login and signup links. Only email_link accounts support a nonempty list. Keep login_url on the public app entry; origins must be canonical HTTP(S) origins without credentials, paths, queries or fragments.

description.description: When to choose this account: role, plan, tenant and intended journeys

instructions.description: Non-secret login instructions and the expected signed-in state; required for custom login

composal_inbox.description: email_password only: true signs in with a Composal-provisioned email address (reused if already provisioned) whose mail people and agents can read, ignoring username; the password may be saved later, after signing up with that address, and the account is not configured until then. false returns to the sent username. Omitted keeps the current choice. email_link accounts always use one; true is rejected for other login methods.

composal_managed_google.description: Select the Composal-managed Google test account when available.

composal_inbox_user.description: The user part of a new Composal address, which becomes <user>@<organization slug>.mailposal.com. Omit it to have one suggested from the name. Only names a new address: an existing address cannot be renamed.

password.description: Required for email_password and other password methods, except an email_password account that uses a Composal address

totp_secret.description: Base32 setup key or otpauth URI, not a current one-time code

passkey.description: JSON enrollment artifact for a cloud-managed software passkey; never returned. Provider acceptance must be tested.

cookies.description: Pasted cookies as name=value (Cookie header supported) or name:"value", separated by newlines or semicolons. Requires login_url for the app scope; stored as an encrypted browser session with a 24-hour import expiry. Values are preserved without URL decoding. Maximum 100 cookies and 1 MiB. Mutually exclusive with passkey and browser_session.

browser_session.description: JSON artifact containing scoped app cookies, localStorage and IndexedDB; Google provider cookies and other origins are rejected. Maximum 1 MiB.

oidc.description: Composal sign-in settings for oidc_identity, which only project credentials accept. Send the persona's user part, such as billing-admin, as username; Composal signs in as <user>.<organization slug>@cred.composal.ai. Blank values use the defaults.

provider_id.description: The provider ID configured in the app. Defaults to composal.

auth_url.description: Better Auth path or HTTPS base URL. Defaults to /api/auth on the selected run target. A separately hosted auth server keeps its explicit URL.

client_id.description: The client ID configured in the app; Composal uses it as the token audience. Defaults to composal without an app URL, or the app origin for legacy URL-based setup. Existing client IDs are retained on edits.

sign_in_verified.description: A sign-in check confirmed this account signs in with its current settings

has_inbox.description: Whether Composal provisioned this address and can show the mail it receives

composal_address.description: The Composal address provisioned for this account, kept while it signs in with another username so turning the address back on reuses it. Null until one is provisioned.

issuer_origin.description: Server-assigned OIDC origin, retained when the credential is edited. Older credentials omit it and retain the legacy issuer.

identity_provider.description: For oidc_identity accounts, the Composal issuer the app trusts and the persona settings it must match

email_suffix.description: Every persona signs in as <user> followed by this suffix, for example .acme@cred.composal.ai

persona_user.description: The user part of this persona's address

triage_id.description: The finding triage a dream learned this lesson from

verification_run_id.description: The run whose failed or blocked Scenario an operator taught this note on

disposition.description: retry resubmits this same operation; not_sent needs a new one; sent must not be sent again.

send_blocked_reason.description: Why the run cannot send now; null when it can.

retry_blocked_reason.description: Why an admitted pending operation cannot retry now; null when it can.

csrf_token.description: Sent back as X-Messages-CSRF-Token; useless without the session cookie.

content.description: Plain text with any account link removed

display_content.description: Message text with card links removed

link.description: A link into the app under test; other links stay in content as text.

reply_to.description: Public ID of the visible quoted parent

data.description: Base64 encoded file, maximum 10 MB decoded

download_url.description: Original file; url may be a JPEG preview for HEIC

github_repository.description: GitHub owner/repository associated with this pull request.

concurrency.description: Up to 50 parallel browsers per run, lowered only by an explicit administrator override. Submitted values are ignored; packages do not cap browser parallelism.

project_id.description: Composal project owning this PR Testing configuration.

trigger_label.description: Label whose addition triggers verification when trigger_on_label is enabled.

github_check_enabled.description: Report the Composal Verify check on GitHub pull requests. When false, new commits get no check and open checks are closed as neutral.

demo_videos_enabled.description: Record a short walkthrough of the change and add it to the PR comment. Off by default.

preview_comment_wildcard.description: A preview address with * for the part that changes, such as https://*.vercel.app. Replaces preview_comment_pattern when present; responses carry it when the pattern was written this way.

imessage_number.description: International destination number; blank or null clears it on an added environment.

messaging_tester_number.description: One configured tester number. Copied to each preview; may be overridden locally before preparation.

write_scenarios.description: Draft and validate focused scenarios for each change on its preview. Off by default.

VerifyPullRequestSettingInput.description: The stored-setting shape released CLIs send. Prefer VerifyPullRequestSetupInput.

previews.description: The previews answers this environment can sign in to

hosting_presets.description: Hosting services that build PR previews and the setup answers each needs

ci_preview.description: The latest preview the project's CI handed over, while the saved setting uses CI

setup.description: The project's saved setup as answers, when it has one.

setup_defaults.description: The answers a new setup starts from

ready.description: Run when a draft PR is marked ready.

preview_cleanup_ready.description: The source is closed or merged and unfinished Scenario execution and Discovery have stopped. Worker and application cleanup do not hold its web runtime.

preview_url.description: Most recently supplied preview URL for the current head commit, retained across verification attempts.

current_run.description: Latest verification request if it matches the current head and base, independent of history pagination.

available_tests.description: All active saved scenarios in the configured project, including scenarios outside the automatic selection.

provider.description: Who builds the previews, such as Vercel or GitLab

links.description: hosting: the preview address with * for the part that changes, such as https://deploy-preview-*--shop.netlify.app.

GitPublicationSubmitRequest.description: Uses the receipt's verified graph and target. Explicit revisions and target fields are rejected. Review message, reviewers, labels, draft, and assets retain normal submit semantics.

message.description: Initial durable rich-text description for newly created changes.

reviewers.description: Organization member names or emails to add as reviewers.

remove_reviewers.description: Organization member names or emails to remove as reviewers.

draft.description: On submit, omitted or null means ready; on sync, omitted or null preserves the current draft status.

transfer_refs.description: Immutable receipt-owned refs returned by preparation; transfer each exact Git target before polling readiness.

expected_head_commit_id.description: Observed original Git head of the existing review. Required together with expected_patchset_number when amending.

timezone.description: Default IANA timezone for organization-local schedules such as nightly dreaming.

agents_only.description: Whether this organization uses the agents-only interface; older responses may omit this value.

source_ui_enabled.description: Organization-scoped Source workspace rollout; missing values mean disabled.

source_control_providers.description: Connected source control providers for this organization. Missing values mean no providers are known.

activated_products.description: Products this organization has activated (PRD 144). Activation is what makes a product's surfaces visible; it is neither permission nor entitlement.

can_activate_products.description: Whether the current user may activate a product for this organization: the organization-admin rule the activation endpoint enforces.

shared_agent_personal_accounts_enabled.description: Whether a shared agent may use one person's account for everyone who chats with it. Present only where agent integrations are on.

waitlist_enabled.description: New public signups require waitlist approval when enabled.

openai_sign_in_enabled.description: Whether ChatGPT identity sign-in is configured and enabled for rollout.
